intro.text:
Shirin Ebadi (Persian: شیرین عبادی, romanized: Širin Ebādi; born 22 June 1947) is an Iranian lawyer, former judge, author, university lecturer and human rights activist. A co-founder of the Defenders of Human Rights Center, she received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2003 for her work for democracy and human rights, particularly the rights of women and children. She was the first Iranian and the first Muslim woman to receive the award.
Following the 2009 Iranian presidential election, she remained outside Iran and has lived in exile in London. In March 2026, Reza Pahlavi announced that Ebadi would lead a committee concerned with proposals for transitional justice following a possible political transition in Iran. She was included in the Time 100 list in 2026.
